title: Last Week's Lesson
prompt: And God kept His people safe through every single one!

title: Objectives
lead: At the end of this lesson, the children will be able to:

bullets.text: Understand that God's patience runs out — there is a **final warning**
Know that God **saves His people** in the middle of trouble
See that there is **power in living for Jesus**

title:
"I tell you, now is the time of God's favor,
now is the day of salvation."

body: 13 Then the Lord said to Moses, “Get up early in the morning, confront Pharaoh and say to him, ‘This is what the Lord, the God of the Hebrews, says: Let my people go, so that they may worship me, 14 or this time I will send the full force of my plagues against you and against your officials and your people, so you may know that there is no one like me in all the earth. 18 Therefore, at this time tomorrow I will send the worst hailstorm that has ever fallen on Egypt, from the day it was founded till now. 19 Give an order now to bring your livestock and everything you have in the field to a place of shelter, because the hail will fall on every person and animal that has not been brought in and is still out in the field, and they will die.’”

20 Those officials of Pharaoh who feared the word of the Lord hurried to bring their slaves and their livestock inside. 21 But those who ignored the word of the Lord left their slaves and livestock in the field. 23 When Moses stretched out his staff toward the sky, the Lord sent thunder and hail, and lightning flashed down to the ground. 25 Throughout Egypt hail struck everything in the fields—both people and animals; it beat down everything growing in the fields and stripped every tree. 26 The only place it did not hail was the land of Goshen, where the Israelites were. 27 Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron. “This time I have sinned,” he said. “The Lord is in the right, and I and my people are in the wrong.” 34 But when Pharaoh saw that the rain and hail and thunder had stopped, he sinned again: He and his officials hardened their hearts.

3 So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said to him, “This is what the Lord, the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘How long will you refuse to humble yourself before me? Let my people go, so that they may worship me. 4 If you refuse to let them go, I will bring locusts into your country tomorrow. 5 They will cover the face of the ground so that it cannot be seen. They will devour what little you have left after the hail, including every tree that is growing in your fields.’” 7 Pharaoh’s officials said to him, “How long will this man be a snare to us? Let the people go, so that they may worship the Lord their God. Do you not yet realize that Egypt is ruined?”

8 Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh. “Go, worship the Lord your God,” he said. “But tell me who will be going.” 10 Pharaoh said, “The Lord be with you—if I let you go, along with your women and children! 11 No! Have only the men go and worship the Lord.” Then Moses and Aaron were driven out of Pharaoh’s presence. 13 So Moses stretched out his staff over Egypt, and the Lord made an east wind blow across the land. 14 They covered all the ground until it was black. They devoured all that was left after the hail—everything growing in the fields and the fruit on the trees. Nothing green remained on tree or plant in all the land of Egypt. 20 But the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he would not let the Israelites go.

21 Then the Lord said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward the sky so that darkness spreads over Egypt—darkness that can be felt.” 22 So Moses stretched out his hand toward the sky, and total darkness covered all Egypt for three days. 23 No one could see anyone else or move about for three days. Yet all the Israelites had light in the places where they lived.

24 Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and said, “Go, worship the Lord. Even your women and children may go with you; only leave your flocks and herds behind.” 25 But Moses said, “You must allow us to have sacrifices and burnt offerings to present to the Lord our God. 26 Our livestock too must go with us; not a hoof is to be left behind.” 27 But the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he was not willing to let them go. 28 Pharaoh said to Moses, “Get out of my sight! Make sure you do not appear before me again! The day you see my face you will die.” 29 “Just as you say,” Moses replied. “I will never appear before you again.”

bullets.text: How did God **keep His people safe** each time?
What happens when someone keeps ignoring God's **final warning?**

title: God's Final Warning

body.text: Early one morning, God sent Moses to warn Pharaoh again. Tomorrow, at this very time, the worst hailstorm Egypt had ever seen would fall.
"Bring your animals inside — or the hail will fall on them!"

prompt: God always warns before He acts. He is never late! ⏳

title: Bring Everything Inside!

body.text: Some Egyptians **believed** God's word. They hurried their servants and animals safely inside.
But others ignored the warning and left everything out in the open field.

prompt: When we hear God's word, the wise thing is to obey it right away.

title: Hail and Fire!

body.text: Then it came — huge hailstones and flashing fire crashed down from the sky, all over Egypt!
It was the mightiest storm Egypt had ever seen.

prompt: Can you make a big thunder-clap with your hands? ⚡

title: Safe in Goshen

body.text: But where God's people lived — in Goshen — there was **no hail at all.** Not one stone!
God kept His people completely safe, right in the middle of the storm.

prompt: God can keep you safe even when trouble is all around! 🛡️

title: Pharaoh's Fake Sorry

body.text: Pharaoh called Moses and cried that he was sorry — "Pray to God, please make it stop!" So Moses prayed, and the storm stopped.
But the moment it stopped, Pharaoh hardened his heart **again.**

prompt: Saying "sorry" is not the same as being sorry.

title: Not a Leaf Will Be Left

body.text: God sent Moses again to warn Pharaoh: if he refused, tomorrow locusts would cover the whole land and eat every green thing the hail had left.
They would strip the fields completely bare!

prompt: The one God speaks through is very powerful! ✨

title: Even His Helpers Begged

body.text: Even Pharaoh's own helpers pleaded with him: "How long will this go on? Let the people go before everything is lost!"
But Pharaoh would **not** listen to good advice.

prompt: A wise child listens to godly counsel. 👂

title: The Sky Went Dark

body.text: God sent a wind, and locusts came — so many they covered the ground until it turned **black!**
They ate every plant and every leaf the hail had left. Nothing green remained.

prompt: Can you hop like a little locust? 🦗

title: Only Halfway

body.text: Pharaoh tried a sneaky deal — the men could go and worship, he said, but the women and children must stay behind.
God wants His people **completely** free — not halfway free.

prompt: God's freedom is total. The devil offers only halfway.

title: Darkness You Can Feel

body.text: Moses stretched out his hand, and a thick, heavy darkness covered all of Egypt — darkness you could almost **feel.**
For three whole days no one could see or move about.

prompt: Close your eyes tight. Imagine three whole days like that! 🌑

title: But God's People Had Light

body.text: While all Egypt sat in darkness, God's people in Goshen had **light** in their homes.
God's children live as light in a dark world.

prompt: You can shine God's light wherever you are! 💡

title: Pharaoh's Last No

body.text: Pharaoh was furious. "Get out! If you ever see my face again, you will die!"
But brave Moses stood calm — because God was with him.

prompt: When God is with you, you don't have to be afraid. 🦁

title: Angela's Diary
footer: Today I'm writing about... Stiff-necked Pharaoh!

title: God Is Never Late ⏳

body.text: Teacher said God told Moses EXACTLY when the hail would come — "about this time tomorrow." God knew the very minute! He is never early and never late.
God is never late. Things will play out in my favour.

teacher_note: Exodus 9:18 — God set the hour in advance ("about this time tomorrow"). He is never early, never late; His timing always plays out in His children's favour.

title: Call on the Lord 🙏

body.text: The Egyptians who listened to God's word ran their animals inside — and they were SAVED from the hail! God's word keeps me safe when I obey it.
Whoever calls the name of the Lord will be saved. If I ever call the name of the Lord in trouble, I will be saved.

teacher_note: Exodus 9:19–21 — Those who feared the Lord's word brought their servants and flocks inside and were saved from the hail. Heeding the Lord in trouble is what rescues.

title: Really, Truly Sorry 💧

body.text: Pharaoh said, "I have sinned!" — but he wasn't really sorry. As soon as the storm stopped, he went right back to being stubborn. Saying sorry is not the same as being sorry.
I must be sincere when I ask the Lord for forgiveness.

teacher_note: Exodus 9:27–35 — Pharaoh said "I have sinned… the Lord is right" (9:27), then hardened his heart the moment the hail stopped (9:34–35). Calling yourself a sinner is not the same as being sorry.

title: Listen to Good Advice 👂

body.text: Even Pharaoh's own helpers warned him: "Egypt is ruined — let them go!" But he covered his ears and would not listen. That's how someone heads to trouble.
A child that will perish will ignore godly counsel. Pharaoh's officials warned him, but he would not listen.

teacher_note: Exodus 10:7 — Pharaoh's own officials warned him ("do you not yet realize that Egypt is ruined?") and he would not listen. A child who will perish ignores godly counsel and instruction.

title: Totally Free 🕊️

body.text: Pharaoh said, "Only the men can go" — trying to keep part of God's people. Satan is like that too: he hates it when a child of God gets COMPLETELY free.
Satan, like stubborn Pharaoh, does not like the total freedom of a child of God.

teacher_note: Exodus 10:8–11 — Pharaoh offered a partial deal ("go, but only the men"). Satan, like stubborn Pharaoh, resists the total freedom of a child of God. God's freedom is never partial.

title: God's Word Is Powerful 💪

body.text: Moses said, "Not a leaf will be left!" — and it happened exactly like he said, because he spoke for God. When I walk with God, I am strong too.
When you are bullied in class, you can face the bully and report it, trusting God to deliver you.

teacher_note: Exodus 10:5–6 — Moses could declare "not a hut will remain" because he spoke for God. A child who walks with God can face a bully — and report it — trusting God to deliver.

title: A Light in the Dark 💡

body.text: All Egypt was pitch dark — but God's people had LIGHT in their homes! I live in this dark world, but I carry God's light. I belong to Him, not to the darkness.
I live in this world as light, but I am not of this world that is full of darkness.

teacher_note: Exodus 10:21–23 — Darkness covered Egypt three days, yet Israel had light where they lived. We live IN this dark world as light, but we are not OF it.

title: God Talks to Me 🗣️

body.text: Moses never had to climb a mountain this whole time — God just spoke to him whenever he needed, like a friend. God can speak to me too, and nothing can break that.
God spoke to Moses mouth-to-mouth. He can speak to me too. His relationship with the Lord was never broken.

teacher_note: Cross-cutting (Exodus 9–10 pattern) — Scripture never records Moses summiting a mountain in this stretch; God spoke to him per need, mouth-to-mouth. His relationship with the Lord was never broken — and neither is ours.

title: Now is the day of salvation.
intro: If you are saved, the Lord will protect you and give you total freedom from sin.
But a child who will perish ignores godly counsel — Pharaoh's officials warned him, and he would not listen. Today, I am warning you…

title: Three More Plagues

bullets.text: **Plague 7:** Hail and fire — but not on Goshen!
**Plague 8:** Locusts ate everything — a final warning!
**Plague 9:** Darkness over Egypt — but God's people had light!

prompt: God is patient — but now is the day to say yes! ❤️

subtitle: Keep shining God's light! 🌟
